ask: What is my friend into, musically?
note: quick_facts carries a music slot; distill fills it from their own messages.

ask: Who is this person and how do I know them?
note: how_we_met plus the first message exchanged.

ask: What does this person do for work right now?
note: works_on slot, refreshed by distill as their messages change.

ask: What are they studying, and where?
Who is in their family?
note: family slot; also relationships table for people both of us know.

ask: What are they worried about at the moment?
needs: distill deliberately skips distress; that is a policy, not a gap.

ask: What did they ask me for that I never did?
What advice have they given me?
What is their faith background?
Do they have any health thing I should be gentle about?
needs: only recorded when they volunteered it and it is not a crisis.

ask: What food do they like or avoid?
What is their sport or their exercise?
Where did they grow up?
What is one thing they said that I should not forget?
note: every fact carries the verbatim quote and its date.

ask: Have they ever mentioned wanting to be introduced to someone?
needs: a can_introduce slot exists; the inverse ask is not modelled.

ask: What are they good at that I would not guess?
I am getting coffee with someone in an hour. Brief me.
What did we talk about last time?
What has changed in their life since we last spoke?
needs: history tracks score movement, not a change log of facts.

ask: What should I ask them about?
note: ask_about slot exists for exactly this.

ask: What do we have in common?
needs: no overlap query across two people's facts.

ask: Is there anything I promised them?
Do I owe them money, or they me?
What is the last thing they were excited about?
Am I about to meet someone they have a history with?
needs: relationships table is sparse and undirected.

ask: Who am I losing touch with?
Who was I close to two years ago and never talk to now?
Who is warming up?
Who reached out to me and I never replied?
needs: needs last-inbound versus last-outbound per person.

ask: Who have I been meaning to call?
Which friendships are one-sided right now?
needs: inbound/outbound message ratio is computable but unimplemented.

ask: Who did I meet this semester and never followed up with?
needs: created_at exists; the follow-up gate does not.

ask: Give me five people to text today.
Who should I see in person this week rather than text?
needs: no channel-preference model.

ask: Which of my closest people am I overdue with?
Who do I know at a given company?
Who could introduce me to someone at Anthropic?
Who in my network works in health tech in LA?
note: PeopleRank does this properly in Amber; here it is FTS plus fields.

ask: Who are the most connected people I know?
needs: rank scores closeness to me, not their centrality.

ask: Who did I meet through a given person?
needs: how_we_met is prose, not a foreign key.

ask: Which YC founders do I know?
Who do I know who has done what I am about to do?
Who should I ask about design?
note: in Sept 2026 Caleb texted eleven designers the same question by hand.

ask: Who have I asked for mentorship before?
Which people do I know only through one group chat?
needs: circle membership exists; the exclusivity query does not.

ask: What is this group chat and who is in it?
Which group chats am I actually active in?
needs: no per-circle recency ranking.

ask: Who is in my church community versus my startup community?
Which groups have gone quiet?
needs: circles have no activity scoring.

ask: Who is in a group with me but I have never texted one to one?
needs: computable from circle_members minus direct threads.

ask: Name everyone from a trip or an event.
Whose birthday is coming up?
What should I get them?
note: interests and food slots make this answerable by an agent.

ask: What happened on this day in previous years?
When did we meet?
What anniversaries or hard dates should I remember for someone?
Who did I spend the most time with last month?
needs: rank is weighted, not a raw time tally.

ask: What did I do last Saturday and who with?
Remind me to check on someone in two weeks.
Is anyone in here duplicated?
Are all my messages attributed to the right person?
note: a bug found on 2026-09-09 had 23% of messages attributed to nobody.

ask: Which senders does the store not recognise?
Work out who an unknown number is from context.
Is my data self-consistent?
What is in here that I never confirmed?
needs: source is recorded per observation but not summarised.

ask: Delete everything about one person.
needs: soft delete only; message rows survive.

ask: Which facts are stale?
needs: observations decay in scoring but facts have no freshness surface.

ask: What do I actually know about myself in here?
What story do I tell about a given thing?
What are my own verified numbers?
note: four resume metrics are flagged as invented on purpose.

ask: What have I said I want to do with my life?
What did I try that failed?
What is my writing voice?
needs: second-brain core/voice.md is the real home for this.

ask: Which of my claims cannot be sourced?
What did I believe a year ago that I no longer believe?
needs: self-facts are dated but never diffed.

ask: Draft a text to this person that sounds like me.
needs: voice lives in second-brain, not the store; an agent must read both.

ask: Write a birthday message that references something real.
Who did I send the same copy-pasted message to?
note: in March 2026 one message went to hundreds of people.

ask: Thank someone specifically rather than generically.
Find the conversation where we talked about a thing.
What did this person say about a topic, ever?
Search everything I know for a keyword.
Ask a question in plain English.
Export what I know as markdown I can read.
Show me a dashboard of my whole network.
Pull the full history with one person as a file.
Turn this week's new messages into facts automatically.
Notice a life event in the messages without me logging it.
Keep scores current as conversations happen.
Back up the store somewhere private.
Tell me when the store has drifted from reality.
Import a new contact source without creating duplicates.
note: dedupe catches exact name and email collisions only.

ask: Learn a person's second phone number or email.
Never re-read a message I have already extracted from.
Run the whole maintenance pass unattended.
Who is going through something hard right now?
needs: deliberately not extracted. Facts about other people's crises are not the store's business.

ask: Who showed up for me this year?
note: events capture meals, hangouts and calls.

ask: Who did I let down, and did I make it right?
needs: apologies are in the messages but nothing indexes them.

ask: Who is new in my life and worth investing in?
Am I giving more attention to people who need it or people who are easy?
needs: the most interesting question here and the least tractable.
